newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian shares one pct down on U.S. slide.
newsitem.headline: Australian shares one pct down on U.S. slide.

text.p: AUD US$0.7410 (Fri cl $0.7405) CRB Index cl 235.04 +0.85
*Broad declines in moderate turnover on the back of Friday's U.S. slide. Gold stocks keep rising. Volume 112.99 million, value A$241.33 million, 856 stocks traded, 262 steady, 210 up, 384 down.
The Australian stock market faced broad declines in moderate volume on Monday following Wall Street's 1.6 percent slide on Friday.

By 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), the All Ordinaries index had lost 28.1 points to 2,656.1 in light turnover of 112.99 million shares. The September share price index futures contract was 32 points lower at 2,666, a premium of 9.9 points to the underlying index. "Local issues are not affecting the market much at the moment. It's more weak overseas markets and nervousness ahead of (Federal Reserve Chairman) Alan Greenspan's congress testimony tomorrow. The market is a bit apprehensive," one dealer said.

Others said some investors were cautiously sidelined ahead of domestic second quarter inflation and wage data later this week, hoping for an indication of whether the Reserve Bank of Australia will cut official interest rates further.
Most heavyweight blue chips retreated, but gold shares went against the trend and rose another 1.2 percent after climbing slightly more on Friday.
"Gold was probably oversold and some merchants were caught short," one Melbourne-based dealer said.
Sector giant Normandy Mining gained four cents to A$1.61 while Acacia Resources rose 5.1 cents to A$1.43.
